task_instance: Follow the skill's core deliverable: obtain a Win32 build of BusyBox (busybox.exe) and use it to run standard UNIX command line tools on Windows (e.g. 'busybox.exe --list' and 'busybox.exe ls -1').
blocker_detail: The skill is explicitly Windows-only and states that on UNIX one should stop. This runtime is an air-gapped Linux x86_64 workstation: there is no Windows environment, no PowerShell, no busybox.exe binary bundled next to SKILL.md, and no Windows emulation layer (wine) installed. The skill's own setup step is to download a Win32 busybox.exe build over the network (the download links are redacted placeholders), which is impossible on an offline machine. Since the core deliverable is specifically running a Windows .exe on Windows, and neither a Windows runtime nor the binary nor network access to fetch it is available, the central intent cannot be exercised here.
evidence: Read SKILL.md: it is titled busybox-on-windows and instructs 'Use this skill only on Windows. If you are on UNIX, then stop here.' Setup requires PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest downloads of busybox.exe from redacted URL placeholders ([url-1]..[url-4]). Checked platform: 'uname -a' => Linux vm ... x86_64 GNU/Linux (not Windows). Listed the skill directory: only SKILL.md present, no busybox.exe bundled. Checked for tooling: 'command -v busybox busybox.exe wine' returned nothing (exit 1) - none installed. No network is available to download the Win32 binary and the links are placeholders. Therefore the Windows-only deliverable (running busybox.exe --list / busybox.exe ls -1) cannot be produced or verified on this offline Linux runtime.
